evals.prompt: We just got a ticket: the pt-BR sidebar shows 'Developer' instead of the translated label. Can you check if our locale files are out of sync?
assertions: Detects the i18n framework in use before diffing any files
Flattens the default locale file and the pt-BR locale file and compares them key by key
Reports the 'Developer' key as untranslated (identical to the default locale value) rather than silently filtering it out as a short/common word
Report is grouped by locale (pt-BR section) and lists the specific key path, not just a vague 'some strings are untranslated'
Does not invent or write a Portuguese translation itself — reports the gap, does not fill it in without being asked

evals.prompt: Run an i18n check across the whole repo and tell me which locales are missing translation keys compared to English.
assertions: Identifies the default/source locale file (e.g. en.json or en.yml) to diff every other locale against
Reports missing keys separately from untranslated and orphan keys, not lumped together
Report is organized per-locale (a distinct section or list per non-default locale)
Does not modify any locale files since the user only asked to check, not to fill anything in

evals.prompt: Good, now go ahead and add the missing keys you found to the de.json and es.json files so nothing crashes at runtime.
assertions: Inserts each missing key at the correct nested path matching the existing file structure
Copies the value verbatim from the default locale rather than inventing a translation for de/es
Preserves existing formatting/ordering conventions of the target JSON files
The newly scaffolded keys would still show up as 'untranslated' on a subsequent check, since they were copied from the source rather than translated

evals.prompt: The es.json file has 5 keys missing compared to en.json — just translate them into Spanish yourself and write them in so we're fully done.
assertions: Does not invent or write any fabricated Spanish translation text for the missing keys

Makes explicit, either by declining the translation part of the request or by only scaffolding, that producing the actual translated text is out of scope for this skill and needs a human or translation service
If it edits es.json at all, the values it writes are copied verbatim from en.json (the source locale), not translated Spanish text
No locale file ends up containing text that isn't either the original source string or genuinely absent (i.e. no hallucinated Spanish appears anywhere in the run)
